sources.title: Why do people eat the same breakfast every day? Goals and circadian rhythms of variety seeking in meals.
sources.sample_or_unit: N=4481 across diary, event reconstruction and experiments
sources.observed_result: Lunch/dinner show greater food variety seeking than breakfast; hedonic goals vary by meal.
sources.hillink_use: Meal-time interaction and repeated-food category experiment, opt-in only.
sources.not_applicable: Not Korean hotel-specific; no venue probabilities or engine coefficients.
sources.applicable: Meal-time variety tendencies, only when personal food evidence is insufficient.

sources.title: Revisit and satiation patterns: Are your restaurant customers satiated?
sources.population: US upscale and casual restaurant customers
sources.sample_or_unit: Questionnaire; sample size not available in accessed abstract; 2/6-week windows
sources.observed_result: Satiation differed with visit frequency, restaurant type and self-control.
sources.hillink_use: C only: bounded repeated-venue term; 48-hour transfer explicitly unvalidated.
sources.not_applicable: Does not establish that a specific person dislikes repetition or quantify 2-day hotel effect.
sources.applicable: Repeated restaurant visits; transfer from 2/6 weeks to a 48-hour stay is an explicitly unvalidated experiment.

sources.title: How does the consumer choose a restaurant? An overview of the determinants of consumer satisfaction.
sources.population: International restaurant consumer studies; countries not fully enumerated in accessible abstract
sources.observed_result: Food, atmosphere, service, price/value and consumer/company factors interact with dining context.
sources.hillink_use: Coverage review only: existing M4 food/space/value terms retained.
sources.not_applicable: No extra generic food/space score: would duplicate M4.
sources.applicable: Review of the dimensions already represented by M4, not new coefficients.
